rows.note: Use this everyday choice when the conclusion is apparent from clues, behavior, or other observable evidence.

example.english: I can infer that you are tired today; you have hardly said anything all morning.
example.traditional: 睇得出你今日好攰，成朝都冇乜出聲。
example.jyutping: tai2 dak1 ceot1 nei5 gam1 jat6 hou2 gui6 sing4 ziu1 dou1 mou5 mat1 ceot1 seng1

rows.note: Use this when the conclusion is tentative or is framed more like a guess.

example.english: Just from hearing your voice, I can infer that you have been drinking.
example.traditional: 淨係聽你把聲，我都估到你飲咗酒。
example.jyutping: zing6 hai6 teng1 nei5 baa2 seng1 ngo5 dou1 gu2 dou3 nei5 jam2 zo2 zau2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose direct equivalent for an explicit, reasoned deduction, especially in careful or written language.

example.english: Based on the traces left at the scene, the police infer that the thief entered through the back door.
example.traditional: 根據現場留下嘅痕跡，警方推斷賊人係由後門入屋。
example.jyutping: gan1 geoi3 jin6 coeng4 lau4 haa6 ge3 han4 zik1 ging2 fong1 teoi1 dyun3 caak6 jan4 hai6 jau4 hau6 mun4 jap6 uk1
